sentences.en: Hi, this is Kaitlin Luna, host of Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是凯特琳·卢纳，是《心理学谈话》节目的主持人。

sentences.en: This podcast was recorded live during the 2018 APA convention in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 本期播客是在旧金山举行的2018年美国心理学会（APA）年会上现场录制的。

sentences.en: This episode is about how our memories may not be as reliable as we'd like to think.
sentences.zh: 本期节目探讨的是我们的记忆可能并不像我们想象的那样可靠。

sentences.en: As always, we want to hear from you, so please email me at kluna at apa.org if you have any comments or ideas for us.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我们期待听到您的声音，如果您有任何意见或想法，请发送电子邮件至kluna@apa.org与我联系。

sentences.en: That's kluna at apa.org.
sentences.zh: That's kluna at apa.org.

sentences.en: I'm joined by Dr. Elizabeth Loftus, a distinguished professor at the University of California, Irvine.
sentences.zh: 今天做客节目的是加州大学欧文分校的杰出教授伊丽莎白·洛夫特斯博士。

sentences.en: Dr. Loftus is well known for her research on human memory, notably false memories.
sentences.zh: 洛夫特斯博士以其在人类记忆，特别是虚假记忆方面的研究而闻名。

sentences.en: Dr. Loftus has been honored by APA's
sentences.zh: 洛夫特斯博士曾被美国心理学会的

sentences.en: Review of General Psychology as one of the 100 most eminent psychologists of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 《普通心理学评论》评为20世纪100位最杰出的心理学家之一。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Loftus.
sentences.zh: 欢迎您，洛夫特斯博士。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: It's wonderful to have you here today.
sentences.zh: 很高兴您今天能来。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: So your research tells us something I would think is unsettling about our minds, that our memories aren't set in stone, that they're basically subject to manipulation.
sentences.zh: 您的研究揭示了一个我认为令人不安的事实，即我们的记忆并非一成不变，而是很容易受到操纵。

sentences.en: So can you explain that a bit more?
sentences.zh: 您能详细解释一下吗？

sentences.en: One of the things that I and other people who do similar work have shown is that once you
sentences.zh: 我和其他从事类似研究的人已经证明，一旦你

sentences.en: have an experience and you record it in memory, it doesn't just stick there in some pristine
sentences.zh: 有了某种经历并将其记录在记忆中，它并不会以某种原始的

sentences.en: form, you know, waiting to be played back like a recording device, but rather new information,
sentences.zh: 形式保存在那里，等着像录音设备一样被回放。相反，新的信息、

sentences.en: new ideas, new thoughts, suggestive information, misinformation, can enter people's conscious awareness and cause a contamination, a distortion, an alteration in memory.
sentences.zh: 新的想法、新的念头、暗示性的信息、错误的信息，都可能进入人们的意识，导致记忆的污染、扭曲和改变。

sentences.en: And that's the kind of thing that I've been studying for the past many decades.
sentences.zh: 这正是我过去几十年来一直在研究的课题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And how can human memories be manipulated?
sentences.zh: 那么人类的记忆是如何被操纵的呢？

sentences.en: They can be manipulated when people talk to each other after, let's say, some crime is over that they may have both witnessed.
sentences.zh: 当人们在某起犯罪事件发生后进行交谈时，如果他们都目击了该事件，记忆就可能被操纵。

sentences.en: They can be manipulated when they are interrogated by an investigator who maybe has an agenda or has a hypothesis about what probably happened and communicates that to the
sentences.zh: 当他们受到调查人员的审讯时，如果调查人员带有某种预设目标或假设，并无意中将这些想法传达给

sentences.en: witness even inadvertently.
sentences.zh: 目击者，记忆也可能被操纵。

sentences.en: People can be manipulated when they see media coverage about an event.
sentences.zh: 当人们看到关于某事件的媒体报道时，也可能受到操纵。

sentences.en: Let's say it's a high publicity event that is talked about a lot on television or newspapers.
sentences.zh: 假设这是一个在电视或报纸上被广泛讨论的高调事件。

sentences.en: In all of these cases, the opportunity is there for new information, not necessarily accurate information, to contaminate a person's memory.
sentences.zh: 在所有这些情况下，都有可能出现新的、不一定准确的信息，从而污染一个人的记忆。

sentences.en: And what got you interested in this work?
sentences.zh: 是什么让您对这项研究产生了兴趣？

sentences.en: Oh, gosh.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: I got interested in studying memory distortion many decades ago.
sentences.zh: 我几十年前就开始对研究记忆扭曲感兴趣了。

sentences.en: As a graduate student, I'd done a little bit of work on human memory.
sentences.zh: 作为一名研究生，我做过一些关于人类记忆的研究。

sentences.en: And then once I got my PhD, I wanted to do some work that had a more immediate practical application.
sentences.zh: 拿到博士学位后，我想做一些具有更直接实际应用价值的工作。

sentences.en: And so I thought, well, I know something about memory, but how about looking at the memory of witnesses to accidents, crimes, and other legally relevant events?
sentences.zh: 于是我想，我对记忆有所了解，那何不研究一下事故、犯罪和其他法律相关事件目击者的记忆呢？

sentences.en: So I kind of combined an interest in legal issues with some expertise in human memory and produced this line of work.
sentences.zh: 所以我将对法律问题的兴趣与人类记忆方面的专业知识结合起来，开展了这项研究。

sentences.en: Can you take us back to the early 1990s when you talk about the memory wars?
sentences.zh: 您能带我们回到20世纪90年代，谈谈所谓的“记忆战争”吗？

sentences.en: So what was that time like and what was happening?
sentences.zh: 那段时期是什么样的？当时发生了什么？

sentences.en: Oh, gee, that, well, in the 1990s, and even in maybe the late 80s, we began to see an altogether more extreme kind of memory problem.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪，在90年代，甚至可能在80年代末，我们开始看到一种更为极端的记忆问题。

sentences.en: Some patients were going into therapy, maybe they were, had anxiety, or maybe they had an eating disorder, or maybe they were depressed.
sentences.zh: 一些患者在接受治疗时，可能患有焦虑症、饮食失调或抑郁症。

sentences.en: And they would end up with a therapist who said something like, well, you know, many people I've seen with your symptoms were sexually abused as a child.
sentences.zh: 他们最终遇到的治疗师会说：“你知道，我见过的许多有你这种症状的人，在童年时期都曾遭受过性虐待。”

sentences.en: And there would begin these activities that would lead these patients to start to think they
sentences.zh: 随后便开始了一系列活动，引导这些患者开始认为他们

sentences.en: remembered years of brutalization that they had allegedly banished into the unconscious until this
sentences.zh: 记得多年来遭受的残酷对待，而这些记忆据称已被他们压抑到潜意识中，直到这次

sentences.en: This therapy made them aware of it.
sentences.zh: 治疗让他们意识到这一点。

sentences.en: And in many instances, these people sued their parents or got their former neighbors or doctors or teachers, whatever, prosecuted based on these claims of repressed memory.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，这些人基于这些压抑记忆的说法，起诉了他们的父母，或者让以前的邻居、医生或老师等人受到了起诉。

sentences.en: So the wars were really about whether people can take years of brutalization,
sentences.zh: 所以，这场战争实际上是关于人们是否能够将多年的残酷对待，

sentences.en: banish it into the unconscious, be completely unaware that these things happen, and then reliably recover all this information later.
sentences.zh: 压抑到潜意识里，完全不知道这些事情发生过，然后又在后来可靠地恢复所有这些信息。

sentences.en: And that was what was so controversial and disputed.
sentences.zh: 这正是最具争议和分歧的地方。

sentences.en: And your work essentially refuted that, that it's not necessarily possible, or maybe brought up to light that this isn't...
sentences.zh: 您的工作基本上反驳了这一点，即这不一定是可能的，或者说揭示了这并不是……

sentences.en: Well, my work actually provided an alternative explanation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的工作实际上提供了一种替代性的解释。

sentences.en: Where could these reports be coming from if this didn't happen?
sentences.zh: 如果这些事情没有发生，那么这些报告是从哪里来的呢？

sentences.en: So my work showed that you could plant very rich, detailed, false memories in the minds of people.
sentences.zh: 我的研究表明，你可以在人们的脑海中植入非常丰富、详细的虚假记忆。

sentences.en: It didn't mean that repressed memories did not exist, and repressed memories could still exist, and false memories could still exiSt.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着压抑记忆不存在，压抑记忆可能依然存在，虚假记忆也可能存在。

sentences.en: But there really wasn't any strong, credible scientific support for this idea of massive repression.
sentences.zh: 但对于这种大规模压抑的观点，确实没有任何强有力、可信的科学支持。

sentences.en: And yet so many families were destroyed by this, what I would say, unsupported claim.
sentences.zh: 然而，许多家庭却因为这种我认为缺乏支持的说法而破裂了。

sentences.en: And going off on what you just said, you were at one point sued by a woman who claimed that her mother sexually abused her.
sentences.zh: 顺着您刚才说的话，您曾被一位声称母亲对她进行性虐待的女性起诉。

sentences.en: And in this situation, you believed the mother had not done this abuse.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，您认为这位母亲并没有实施这种虐待。

sentences.en: And you published, and you called it an expose, and it was controversial, and you were sued by this daughter.
sentences.zh: 您发表了一篇文章，称其为揭露报道，这引起了争议，您也被这位女儿起诉了。

sentences.en: And you talked about, in your TED talk, you talked about the disturbing trend of scientists being sued for their work.
sentences.zh: 您在TED演讲中谈到了科学家因其工作而被起诉的令人不安的趋势。

sentences.en: So can you speak a little bit about that, and what is that, as a scientist, what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 您能谈谈这一点吗？作为一名科学家，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: There was a case history that was floating around in the literature, published by a psychiatriSt.
sentences.zh: 当时文献中流传着一个由精神科医生发表的案例记录。

sentences.en: And it was being used as the new proof of massive repression.
sentences.zh: 它被用作大规模压抑的新证据。

sentences.en: The case history was anonymous, so it was Jane Doe and John Doe, Mom's Town, Dad's Town.
sentences.zh: 该案例记录是匿名的，所以是简·多伊和约翰·多伊，妈妈的城镇，爸爸的城镇。

sentences.en: And at some point, I was able to identify the Doe family.
sentences.zh: 后来，我设法确定了多伊一家。

sentences.en: And once I found the Doe family, the name of the family, then I could get into the divorce file,
sentences.zh: 一旦我找到了多伊一家，找到了这个家庭的名字，我就能查阅离婚档案，

sentences.en: and I found all kinds of information that had been left out of this psychiatrist's account.
sentences.zh: 我发现了所有被这位精神科医生的叙述所遗漏的信息。

sentences.en: And I found enough information to convince me that there was a very strong likelihood that this accused mother, oddly the mother accused of sexual abuse, was probably innocent.
sentences.zh: 我发现的信息足以让我相信，这位被指控的母亲——奇怪的是，被指控性虐待的母亲——很可能是无辜的。

sentences.en: And just being involved in this investigation got me in a lot of hot water.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是参与这项调查就让我陷入了巨大的麻烦。

sentences.en: So, yes, the adult daughter did sue me and sue my co-author and the magazine where we published the expose and some other people.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，那位成年女儿确实起诉了我，还起诉了我的合著者、我们发表揭露报道的杂志以及其他一些人。

sentences.en: And eventually, after years, the litigation ended.
sentences.zh: 最终，经过多年的诉讼，案件结束了。

sentences.en: And you won the, in 2016, you won the John Maddox Prize, which recognizes the work of scientists who promote science and evidence,
sentences.zh: 您在2016年获得了约翰·马多克斯奖，该奖项旨在表彰那些促进科学和证据，

sentences.en: but might face difficulty in doing so or hostility.
sentences.zh: 但在此过程中可能面临困难或敌意的科学家。

sentences.en: So, can you talk a little bit about that and why you believe it's important to speak out, even when it's difficult,
sentences.zh: 您能谈谈这一点，以及为什么您认为即使在困难的情况下，也要站出来说话很重要，

sentences.en: even when you face these tough situations where you might be sued or your name gets called out and dragged through the mud, that sort of thing?
sentences.zh: 即使您面临这些艰难的处境，可能会被起诉，或者名字被点名并被抹黑，诸如此类的事情？

sentences.en: Well, I did win the John Maddox Prize, and I'm very proud of that, because it is a recognition of standing up for science and in the face of a lot of hostility.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我确实获得了约翰·马多克斯奖，我对此感到非常自豪，因为它认可了在面对大量敌意时坚持科学的行为。

sentences.en: And the hostility came not just from a lawsuit or, you know, but other individuals who were feeling, I guess,
sentences.zh: 这种敌意不仅来自诉讼，还有其他一些人，我想他们觉得

sentences.en: that their cherished beliefs were being attacked and would lash out in all kinds of unpleasant, unpleasant ways.
sentences.zh: 他们珍视的信仰受到了攻击，于是以各种令人不快的方式进行抨击。

sentences.en: But I do think it's important because, I mean, science, you know, is that candle in the dark.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为这很重要，因为科学是黑暗中的蜡烛。

sentences.en: And, you know, it is the thing that's going to help make this a better world.
sentences.zh: 它是让这个世界变得更美好的东西。

sentences.en: So, and it needs to be protected, especially in today's climate.
sentences.zh: 所以，它需要被保护，特别是在当今的氛围下。

sentences.en: Can you talk about the ethical questions that have come up about your research and how you've responded?
sentences.zh: 您能谈谈关于您的研究中出现的伦理问题以及您是如何回应的吗？

sentences.en: I'll say that again.
sentences.zh: 我再说一遍。

sentences.en: Can you talk about the, can you speak to the ethical questions that have come up about your research and how you've responded over the years?
sentences.zh: 您能谈谈多年来关于您的研究中出现的伦理问题以及您是如何回应的吗？

sentences.en: The ethical questions.
sentences.zh: 伦理问题。

sentences.en: Well, I suppose one ethical question is whether, what I do in my experiments is plant false memories in the minds of people in order to study the process.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想一个伦理问题是，我在实验中所做的是为了研究过程而在人们脑海中植入虚假记忆。

sentences.en: It's little bitty false memories and then great big ones.
sentences.zh: 有很小的虚假记忆，也有很大的虚假记忆。

sentences.en: So, some people might think that that's not a very ethical thing to do.
sentences.zh: 所以，有些人可能会认为这不是一件很道德的事情。

sentences.en: But, number one, everything is reviewed by the human subjects review committees at the universities.
sentences.zh: 但首先，一切都经过了大学人类受试者审查委员会的审查。

sentences.en: Many people have done these same kinds of experiments.
sentences.zh: 许多人都做过同样的实验。

sentences.en: As far as I know, there's never been an adverse effect.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，从未产生过任何负面影响。

sentences.en: And it has been a scientific contribution that I think has helped make the world a better place.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一种科学贡献，我认为它有助于让世界变得更美好。

sentences.en: And you've spoken about the positives of planting false memories, like how it can be used in a positive way.
sentences.zh: 您曾谈到植入虚假记忆的积极方面，比如它如何能以积极的方式被使用。

sentences.en: Can you elaborate a little more on that and what you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 您能详细说明一下吗？您指的是什么？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: One little twist in the false memory work that we did is to look at the consequences of having a false memory.
sentences.zh: 我们在虚假记忆研究中做的一个小转折是观察拥有虚假记忆的后果。

sentences.en: If I plant a false memory in you, does it have ripple effects?
sentences.zh: 如果我在你脑海中植入一个虚假记忆，它会有连锁反应吗？

sentences.en: Does it affect your later thoughts or your later intentions or your later behavior?
sentences.zh: 它会影响你以后的想法、意图或行为吗？

sentences.en: And we've now shown that you can plant a false memory that you got sick eating a particular food.
sentences.zh: 我们现在已经证明，你可以植入一个虚假记忆，让你觉得吃某种食物生病了。

sentences.en: You got sick on pickles or eggs or strawberry ice cream and you don't want to eat as much of that food.
sentences.zh: 你因为吃酸黄瓜、鸡蛋或草莓冰淇淋而生病，然后你就不想吃那么多那种食物了。

sentences.en: We've planted false memories that you got sick drinking a vodka drink and you're not as interested in a vodka drink.
sentences.zh: 我们植入了你喝伏特加酒生病的虚假记忆，你就对伏特加酒不那么感兴趣了。

sentences.en: We've done the opposite, planted a warm fuzzy memory that you loved a healthy food, asparagus in our study.
sentences.zh: 我们做了相反的实验，植入了一种温暖、模糊的记忆，让你爱上一种健康食品，比如我们研究中的芦笋。

sentences.en: And people want to eat more asparagus.
sentences.zh: 人们就想吃更多的芦笋。

sentences.en: So if we can control people's nutritional selections and maybe help them live a healthier life, maybe that's not a bad thing to do.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们能控制人们的营养选择，也许能帮助他们过上更健康的生活，这也许不是一件坏事。

sentences.en: Is there any dangers to planting false memories, even if it is for something positive, like you're trying to eat healthier or lose weight or something like that?
sentences.zh: 植入虚假记忆是否有任何危险，即使是为了积极的事情，比如你想吃得更健康或减肥之类的？

sentences.en: Well, the danger, I guess the danger is that some evil, nefarious people could take this mine technology and put it to some bad use.
sentences.zh: 嗯，危险在于，我想危险在于一些邪恶、卑劣的人可能会利用这种思维技术去做坏事。

sentences.en: Just the way we can build a nuclear bomb now and put it to some bad use.
sentences.zh: 就像我们现在可以制造核弹并将其用于坏事一样。

sentences.en: Can you talk about the broad implications of your research on criminal law?
sentences.zh: 您能谈谈您的研究对刑法的广泛影响吗？

sentences.en: I think that the work that I and many other people have done on human memory, eyewitness testimony, the memory of witnesses and victims to crimes,
sentences.zh: 我认为我和许多其他人所做的人类记忆、目击者证词、犯罪目击者和受害者的记忆研究，

sentences.en: has had some impact on the legal system.
sentences.zh: 对法律体系产生了一些影响。

sentences.en: The scientific studies have revealed something that we might call best practices that have been implemented in a number of jurisdictions so that when law enforcement members of the legal system interact with people who are involved in legal cases,
sentences.zh: 科学研究揭示了一些我们可以称之为“最佳实践”的方法，这些方法已在许多司法管辖区实施，以便当执法人员与法律案件相关人员互动时，

sentences.en: they get the most accurate and complete information from people.
sentences.zh: 他们能从人们那里获得最准确、最完整的信息。

sentences.en: And we aren't wrongly convicting people of crimes they didn't do.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就不会错误地给没有犯罪的人定罪。

sentences.en: So I see some great impact there.
sentences.zh: 所以我看到了很大的影响。

sentences.en: Is there anything we can do to prevent against false memories or to enhance our memories?
sentences.zh: 我们有什么办法可以预防虚假记忆或增强我们的记忆力吗？

sentences.en: Oh, you know, if you warn people that somebody might be trying to mislead them or fool them, they can momentarily protect themselves and kind of fend off the misinformation.
sentences.zh: 噢，你知道，如果你警告人们有人可能试图误导或愚弄他们，他们可以暂时保护自己，抵御错误信息。

sentences.en: The problem is that people don't walk around in life with those warnings at the forefront of their consciousness.
sentences.zh: 问题是，人们在生活中并不会时刻带着这些警告。

sentences.en: And so we're going to need to find some other ways of getting people to protect themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要找到其他方法来让人们保护自己。

sentences.en: And can you enhance your memory?
sentences.zh: 那么你能增强你的记忆力吗？

sentences.en: Like, can you, you know, to ensure that maybe the information you do remember is more accurate or is it even possible?
sentences.zh: 比如，你能确保你记住的信息更准确吗？或者这可能吗？

sentences.en: There are things you can do to enhance your memory for usually two simple things are just to pay better attention at the time you're being experiencing something or learning somebody's name at a party,
sentences.zh: 你可以做一些事情来增强记忆力，通常两件简单的事情就是：在你经历某事或在聚会上学习某人的名字时，更加专注，

sentences.en: for example, and then rehearsal.
sentences.zh: 例如，然后是复述。

sentences.en: And certainly we know the best patterns of rehearsal that are known to maximize the likelihood that people will remember the information.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们知道最好的复述模式，这些模式已知能最大程度地提高人们记住信息的可能性。

sentences.en: Just as we spoke about prepping for your TED talk, you said you took many months to prep for memorizing a 16-minute talk.
sentences.zh: 正如我们谈到为您的TED演讲做准备时，您说您花了几个月的时间来准备背诵一个16分钟的演讲。

sentences.en: So it's a lot of work to memorize something that long and to enhance your memory.
sentences.zh: 所以背诵那么长的内容并增强记忆力需要做很多工作。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, I'd been teaching for decades when I was invited to do a TED talk at TED Global.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道，当我被邀请在TED Global做演讲时，我已经教书几十年了。

sentences.en: And so this was going to be a talk in front of maybe a thousand people in the audience and then it would go out on the TED website and it would be translated into who knows how many languages.
sentences.zh: 所以这将是在大约一千名观众面前进行的演讲，然后它会发布在TED网站上，并被翻译成不知道多少种语言。

sentences.en: So the exact wording was part of it and you have to memorize it and it actually took me about three months to, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以确切的措辞是其中的一部分，你必须背下来，我实际上花了大约三个月的时间，你知道，

sentences.en: practicing and talking to the mirror and talking to trees to get it down.
sentences.zh: 练习，对着镜子说话，对着树说话，才把它记下来。

sentences.en: And I used a few tricks that I'd learned as a memory scientist, like the method of loci.
sentences.zh: 我用了一些我作为记忆科学家学到的技巧，比如“轨迹法”。

sentences.en: And so I could even give you the talk right now, even though it's been five years.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在甚至可以给你做那个演讲，尽管已经过去五年了。

sentences.en: What are some of those methods you said?
sentences.zh: 您说的那些方法有哪些？

sentences.en: I mean, it's obviously repetition.
sentences.zh: 我是说，显然是重复。

sentences.en: No, the method of loci involves taking a chunk of material that you want to remember and placing it in a spot, let's say in your home,
sentences.zh: 不，轨迹法涉及选取你想要记住的一块材料，并将其放置在一个地点，比如在你的家里，

sentences.en: and then the next chunk in another spot and the next chunk in another spot.
sentences.zh: 然后下一块放在另一个地点，再下一块放在另一个地点。

sentences.en: And then you take a mental walk through your home and you see the chunks.
sentences.zh: 然后你在脑海中穿过你的家，你就能看到这些材料。

sentences.en: So, for example, I'd like to tell you about a case I worked on involving a man named Steve Titus.
sentences.zh: 例如，我想告诉你一个我处理过的案件，涉及一个叫史蒂夫·泰特斯的人。

sentences.en: Titus was a restaurant manager.
sentences.zh: 泰特斯是一位餐厅经理。

sentences.en: And one day he was accused of a horrible crime.
sentences.zh: 有一天，他被指控犯下了一起可怕的罪行。

sentences.en: So I remember that because I walked to my front door and there is Steve Titus.
sentences.zh: 所以我记得那个，因为我走到我的前门，那里有史蒂夫·泰特斯。

sentences.en: OK, tell him about Titus.
sentences.zh: 好的，告诉他关于泰特斯的事。

sentences.en: And then I go into my house and there's a portrait over here of that my mother in law did when I married her son.
sentences.zh: 然后我走进我的房子，这里有一幅肖像画，是我嫁给她儿子时我婆婆画的。

sentences.en: And I look at tell him about you.
sentences.zh: 我看着它，告诉他关于你的事。

sentences.en: You know, then there's some pine cones over here.
sentences.zh: 你知道，然后这里有一些松果。

sentences.en: That's the wrongly accused.
sentences.zh: 那是被错误指控的人。

sentences.en: Tell him about the wrongly accused.
sentences.zh: 告诉他关于被错误指控的人的事。

sentences.en: So in walking through a familiar location where you've placed chunks of what you need to remember, you can master it.
sentences.zh: 所以，通过走过一个你放置了需要记住的内容的熟悉地点，你就能掌握它。

sentences.en: That's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: I definitely need to work on that.
sentences.zh: 我绝对需要练习一下那个。

sentences.en: Well, there's a fabulous book called Moonwalking with Einstein that describes this whole method.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一本很棒的书叫《与爱因斯坦月球漫步》，描述了整个方法。

sentences.en: It's really a great popular book.
sentences.zh: 这真是一本很棒的科普书。

sentences.en: That's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 那太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much for joining us, Dr. Loftus.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢您加入我们，洛夫特斯博士。

sentences.en: I really appreciate your time today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您今天抽出时间。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is part of the APA Podcast Network,
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》是美国心理学会（APA）播客网络的一部分，

sentences.en: which includes other great podcasts like APA Journals Dialogue about the latest and most exciting psychological research and progress notes about the practice of psychology.
sentences.zh: 该网络还包括其他优秀的播客，例如探讨最新、最令人兴奋的心理学研究的《APA期刊对话》，以及关于心理学实践的《进度笔记》。

sentences.en: You can find our podcasts on iTunes, Stitcher or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 您可以在iTunes、Stitcher或任何您获取播客的地方找到我们的节目。

sentences.en: You can also visit speakingofpsychology.org to find more episodes and resources on the topics we discuss.
sentences.zh: 您也可以访问speakingofpsychology.org，查找我们所讨论主题的更多剧集和资源。

sentences.en: I'm your host, Caitlin Luna for the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人凯特琳·卢娜，代表美国心理学会。
